messages.content:
RoadDraft is a headless 2D CAD engine for roadway plans. Model space is US survey feet, and a point is [x, y] = [easting, northing] -- the other way round from how coordinates are usually spoken, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]. Sheets are paper inches seen through viewports at a feet-per-inch scale. Work through the commands: each one validates its params and explains what was wrong, every change is journaled and undoable. Start with get_document_state to see what is in the document, list_commands for the full surface, and render_sheet or render_model to look at your work.

To annotate something, find it before you point at it. In a sheet file the design usually lives in a referenced basefile, so the document owns no geometry of its own; find_entities searches the attachments too. Filter by what a thing IS -- layer, type, or its design anchor -- rather than dumping the document: find_entities {anchor: {kind: 'offset', offset: [-15, 15]}, visible_on: 'P-202'} is the pavement edges that sheet shows. Then pass the id straight to place_callout as target_entity, and the engine puts the leader tip on the geometry. Do not compute the point yourself: the midpoint of a curve's endpoints is not on the curve, and roadway linework runs parallel a few feet apart, so a hand-computed point usually lands on the wrong line rather than on nothing. If you do pass a raw target point, read the warning that comes back -- it names what the tip actually touched.

Some things are not entities at all -- a station, a PC, a point at an offset. Ask the design for those: list_alignments with include_references=true names a referenced alignment 'BASE:RTE-7', and station_to_xy, xy_to_station, resolve_anchor and get_design_data all accept that name and answer in host coordinates. To call one out, give place_callout a target_anchor ('86+50@15R', 'PC-2'; BC-2 and EC-2 name the PC and PT too) and that alignment name. Otherwise commands do not take it: nothing can be drawn, labelled or anchored to an alignment this document does not own.

Plan annotation belongs on the sheet, in paper inches, not in the model. Pass the sheet as place_callout's space and still name a model target -- target_entity or target_anchor: the engine sees it through the sheet's viewport (scale and twist included) and puts the tip where it shows on the paper. 'at' then runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, since a pavement edge runs the whole project and a sheet shows one stretch. find_entities with visible_on gives each row a sheet_point, which is where that tip will land -- use it to choose a position for the text that is clear of the linework. Never work out a viewport by hand: model_to_sheet and sheet_to_model convert, and station_to_xy and point_on_entity take a sheet and answer in paper inches as well.

Drafting from a description works the same way: give the engine the description, not coordinates you worked out. A bearing and distance goes in as written -- create_alignment takes start + legs (each leg a bearing, azimuth or deflection and the distance to the next PI, with the radius of the curve at the PI it starts from), draw_traverse draws lines and curves course by course, and traverse computes the points without drawing. offset_entity copies linework parallel at a distance (one entity, or a chain offset as one path), fillet rounds the corner between two lines with a curve (a curb return), and measure with along gives distances along a line, chain or alignment and square off it. key_points and snap give the exact endpoints, intersections, centers and alignment design points (PI, BC, EC) to build on. Station-and-offset drafting is draw_station_offset with the stations and offsets given ('82+00@15R'). Linework drawn through something is cut back with trim (a point on the part to cut away) or run on with extend, not redrawn from computed points; break, join, lengthen, chamfer, copy, rotate, mirror, scale and array edit what is there. create_points sets COGO points, label_segments letters bearings and distances or L1/C1 tags with line and curve tables, place_along sets blocks or points at an interval, hatch fills an area (a point inside is enough), and area and get_entity read areas, lengths, bearings and curve data off the drawing.

Do one drafting task in a headless CAD engine called RoadDraft, using the tools you have been given. They are your ENTIRE tool surface.

Rules:
- Every change to the drawing must go through a tool call.
- The document is already open and saves itself after each command. Do not save it under another name.
- Nobody can answer questions. Work until you judge the task done, then stop and give your report.
- You have no calculator and no code execution. Any arithmetic you need, do yourself.

THE TASK:
Add a right-turn lane to SR-100, on the right side: 12 ft wide, full width from station 31+20 to station 36+00, opened by a 120 ft straight taper that leaves the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00. Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP -- the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge.

When finished, reply briefly with:
1. What you created and drew (names, layers, key coordinates).
2. The tool calls that mattered, in order (tool name + the key arguments).
3. Anything that failed, confused you, or that you had to work around -- quote error messages. If you had to compute coordinates yourself, show the arithmetic.

messages.reasoning:
The user wants to add a right-turn lane to "SR-100" on the right side.
The turn lane has these specifications:
- Width: 12 ft.
- Full width: From station 31+20 to station 36+00.
- Taper: 120 ft straight taper from the existing edge of pavement (EOP) at station 30+00.
- Layer: `rd_EP`.
- Components to draw:
  1. The taper (from 30+00 to 31+20).
  2. The full-width edge (from 31+20 to 36+00).
  3. A square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge (this sounds like a closure or a perpendicular segment).

Wait, let's re-read: "the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge."
A right-turn lane on the right side:
- Existing EOP is the baseline.
- The new EOP will be 12' offset from the existing EOP on the right.
- The taper starts at station 30+00 (where the new EOP is 0' offset from existing EOP).
- The taper ends at station 31+20 (where the new EOP is 12' offset from existing EOP).
- The taper length is 120' (from 30+00 to 31+20 is 120').
- The full-width segment runs from 31+20 to 36+00.
- At 36+00, there is a "square end" back to the existing edge. This means a line perpendicular to the alignment at 36+00, connecting the new EOP to the old EOP.

Wait, the "existing edge of pavement" is a reference. I need to find "SR-100" to know where the alignment is and where the existing EOP is.

Plan:
1. `list_alignments` to find "SR-100".
2. `find_entities` to find the existing EOP for "SR-100". If it's an alignment offset, I might need to find it via `find_entities` with an anchor or just look for linework. Actually, the task implies SR-100 is an alignment. I'll check `list_alignments`.
3. Once I have the alignment, I can use `draw_station_offset` or `draw_offset`.
   - The "taper" is a line from (30+00, 0) to (31+20, 12R).
   - The "full width" is an offset from 31+20 to 36+00 at 12R.
   - The "square end" is a line at 36+00 from offset 12R to 0.

Actually, `draw_station_offset` is perfect for this.
Points for `draw_station_offset`:
1. `30+00@0`
2. `31+20@12R`
3. `36+00@12R`
4. `36+00@0`

Wait, `draw_station_offset` draws the linework. The task says "Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP".
I should check if layer `rd_EP` exists, or just create it. Usually, it's better to create it.

Let's start by finding the alignment.

The task is to add a right-turn lane to `SR-100` on the right side.
Details:
- Width: 12 ft.
- Full width: From station 31+20 to 36+00.
- Opening taper: 120 ft straight taper leaving the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00.
- New edge of pavement layer: `rd_EP`.
- Draw:
    1. The taper (from 30+00 to 31+20).
    2. The full-width edge (from 31+20 to 36+00).
    3. A square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge.

Wait, the instructions say "Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP -- the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge."
This means I need to draw the *new* edge.

Let's analyze the segments of the new edge (on the right side, so offsets are positive):
1. **Taper**: Starts at station 30+00 with offset 0 (the existing edge) and goes to station 31+20 with offset 12. Wait, "leaves the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00". This implies the existing edge is at offset 0 and the new edge starts at 30+00, offset 0, and ends at 31+20, offset 12.
2. **Full Width**: From station 31+20, offset 12, to station 36+00, offset 12.
3. **Square End**: At station 36+00, a line from offset 12 back to offset 0.

Wait, the task says "opened by a 120 ft straight taper".
If it starts at 30+00 and reaches full width at 31+20, the length is 3120 - 3000 = 120 ft. This matches the "120 ft straight taper" description.

So the new edge of pavement consists of:
- Segment 1: Station 30+00, Offset 0 to Station 31+20, Offset 12.
- Segment 2: Station 31+20, Offset 12 to Station 36+00, Offset 12.
- Segment 3: Station 36+00, Offset 12 to Station 36+00, Offset 0.

I should use `draw_station_offset` to create this linework.
`draw_station_offset` allows specifying a sequence of station-and-offset points.
The points are:
1. '30+00@0'
2. '31+20@12'
3. '36+00@12'
4. '36+00@0'

Wait, the existing edge of pavement is at offset 0. The new edge of pavement (the outer edge of the lane) is what I'm drawing.
The taper starts where the lane begins (30+00) and ends when it reaches full width (31+20).
The task says "Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP -- the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge."

Actually, `draw_station_offset` will draw a path. If I provide:
`points = ['30+00@0', '31+20@12', '36+00@12', '36+00@0']`
It will draw:
- A straight line from (30+00, 0) to (31+20, 12).
- A path from (31+20, 12) to (36+00, 12) following the alignment (this will be curved if the alignment is curved).
- A straight line from (36+00, 12) to (36+00, 0).

This exactly describes the "new edge of pavement".

First, I need to create the layer `rd_EP`.

messages.reasoning:
Okay, I see `SR-100` is the alignment.
The task is to add a 12 ft wide right-turn lane on the right side.
It's full width from station 31+20 to 36+00.
It's opened by a 120 ft straight taper that leaves the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00.

Wait, let's clarify the taper.
"opened by a 120 ft straight taper that leaves the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00".
The full width starts at 31+20.
If it's a 120 ft taper starting from 30+00, it ends at 31+20 (30+00 + 120 = 31+20).
So the taper is from station 30+00 to 31+20.
At 30+00, the offset is 0 (the existing edge).
At 31+20, the offset is 12' (the full width of the lane).
Then from 31+20 to 36+00, the offset is 12'.
Then at 36+00, there's a "square end... back to the existing edge".
This means a line from (36+00, 12' R) to (36+00, 0).

The command `draw_station_offset` is perfect for this.
I need the points:
1. '30+00@0' (Existing edge)
2. '31+20@12R' (Start of full width)
3. '36+00@12R' (End of full width)
4. '36+00@0' (Back to existing edge)

Wait, the task says: "Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP -- the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge."
The taper is from 30+00 to 31+20.
The full-width edge is from 31+20 to 36+00.
The square end is at 36+00.

Wait, `draw_station_offset` with `follow=true` will handle the taper and the full width.
If I provide:
'30+00@0', '31+20@12R', '36+00@12R', '36+00@0'
The segment between '30+00@0' and '31+20@12R' will be a straight taper because the offset changes.
The segment between '31+20@12R' and '36+00@12R' will follow the alignment because the offset is constant.
The segment between '36+00@12R' and '36+00@0' will be a straight line perpendicular to the alignment at station 36+00.

Let's verify the stationing.
30+00 is 3000.0.
31+20 is 3120.0.
36+00 is 3600.0.

I will use `draw_station_offset` with `alignment='SR-100'`.
Layer: `rd_EP`.
Points: `['30+00@0', '31+20@12R', '36+00@12R', '36+00@0']`.
Wait, should I use `0` or `0R`? The prompt says "on the right side".
`draw_station_offset` documentation: "station-and-offset points... '@offset' (ft, right +, e.g. 'PC-2@18', '86+50@25L')".
So 12R is correct. For 0, I can just use `0` or `0R`. I'll use `0R` for clarity or just `0`.
Actually, `30+00@0` is on the alignment.
`31+20@12R` is the start of the full width.
`36+00@12R` is the end of the full width.
`36+00@0` is the end of the lane.

Let's check if `rd_EP` layer exists. `create_layer` said it already exists.
I'll proceed with drawing.

messages.content:
I have completed the task of adding the right-turn lane to SR-100.

1. **What I created and drew:**
   - I drew the new edge of pavement on layer `rd_EP`.
   - The linework consists of three segments:
     - A 120.60 ft straight taper from station `30+00` (CL) to station `31+20` (12' RT).
     - A full-width edge of pavement running from station `31+20` (12' RT) to `36+00` (12' RT).
     - A square end at station `36+00` connecting the 12' offset back to the centerline.
   - **Key Coordinates:**
     - `30+00 CL`: [2982.67, 1127.56]
     - `31+20 12' RT`: [3100.30, 1154.12]
     - `36+00 12' RT`: [3555.67, 1305.91]
     - `36+00 CL`: [3551.88, 1317.29]

2. **The tool calls that mattered:**
   - `create_layer(name="rd_EP", ...)`
   - `draw_station_offset(alignment="SR-100", layer="rd_EP", points=["30+00@0", "31+20@12R", "36+00@12R", "36+00@0"])`

3. **Workarounds/Errors:**
   - `create_layer` failed initially because `rd_EP` already existed: `[tool error] { "ok": false, "message": "layer 'rd_EP' already exists" }`. I proceeded using the existing layer.
   - I used `0` offset to represent the centerline for the start and end points of the taper and square end.
